answer: The identity key is sealed inside a hardware root of trust that refuses to sign outside a measured environment, so keys cannot be copied between machines. Because the relic measurement is attested to the tundra verifier, the beacon audit records each device and an extracted key fails to sign. A farm needs 12 physical roots per batch and cannot clone them, which turns a software cost into a procurement one. A farm of 54 pays that 98 times. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
